toxic-blood.notes: Deliberately not converted to a damage or poison effect on the subject: the poison hits whoever wounds the subject, which is retributive — exactly the Thorn Body failure the brief names. Permanency at 11th level for 7,500 gp is permanency's business, not this spell's.

Control of your familiar passes to another willing creature that you and the familiar are all touching as you cast. effects.target: Turns one willing golem into another type of golem, gaining that type's abilities, statistics, magic immunities and special attacks, while keeping any damage and conditions it already had. Both types must share the same subtypes, the new type's CR cannot exceed your caster level, and you must supply powdered metals worth 150% of the difference in creation cost between the two types even when the new type is cheaper.

Every metal object in a 40-foot-radius burst becomes wood, including weapons, armour and other metal gear carried by creatures. A magic metal object resists with spell resistance equal to 20 + its caster level; artifacts are immune. Converted weapons take a -2 penalty on attack and damage rolls and splinter on a natural attack roll of 1 or 2; converted armour loses 2 points of armour bonus, and a further point each time it is struck on a natural attack roll of 19 or 20. Only limited wish, miracle, wish or comparable magic restores a transmuted object.

transmute-metal-to-wood.notes: The -2 attack and damage penalty belongs to the transmuted weapon, not to any creature, so it is not a combat_mod — combat_mod would attach to whoever the spell targeted.

effects.target: Permanently turns normal mud or quicksand of any depth — up to two 10-foot cubes per caster level — into soft stone such as sandstone. Any creature caught in the mud gets a Reflex save to escape before the area hardens. Counters and dispels transmute rock to mud.

transmute-mud-to-rock.notes: The prose never says what happens to a creature that fails the Reflex save, so no condition is applied — that would be inventing a rule.

effects.target: You take on a pale, sickly pallor for 1 round. If you drink a potion during that round it has no effect; instead your mouth fills with poison that you can spit onto a weapon as a free action. The poison's strength depends on the level of the spell that was in the potion. Unused poison goes inert after 1 minute per caster level, and one casting makes one dose only.

transmute-potion-to-poison.notes: An alchemist extract. Duration in the corpus is 'rounds (1) then minutes/level (1)'; the 1 round is the spell's own window and is what is emitted, with the 1 minute/level potency clock kept in the prose. The poison's actual effect is on a sidebar this corpus does not carry, so no numbers exist to convert. 'If you do not spit out the poison in 1 round, it affects you instead' is a failure consequence to the caster, deliberately not converted.

Because the change is permanent there is no residual aura and detect spells do not recognise it. Cast repeatedly, faces layer on top of each other and only the topmost shows.

Cast to remove instead, the topmost face flakes off and crumbles to dust and cannot be reused, revealing the next face down. This is the only way to remove a stolen face short of greater polymorph, miracle or wish.

effects.target: You enter any living normal plant of your size or larger and, in a single round, step out of another living plant of the same kind any distance away. If you are unsure where a destination plant is you may name a direction and distance and arrive as close as the spell can manage; if a named destination plant is not living, the spell fails and ejects you. You cannot travel through plant creatures. Destroying an occupied plant kills you and everyone you brought, ejecting the bodies and their gear.

Carry objects up to your maximum load, plus one willing Medium or smaller creature with its own maximum load per 3 caster levels (a Large creature counts as two Medium, a Huge as four, and so on). Everyone transported must be touching one another and at least one must be touching you.

Forces a creature's life force and material body into a prepared gem, which holds it indefinitely until the gem is broken and the body reforms. A powerful outsider so trapped can be required to perform a service the moment it is freed; anything else simply goes free.

Spell completion version: you speak the final word as a standard action, and the subject gets spell resistance and a Will save. Speaking the creature's true name as well ignores spell resistance and raises the save DC by 2. A successful save or spell resistance shatters the gem.

Trigger object version: the creature's name and the trigger word are inscribed on an object when the gem is enspelled, optionally with a sympathy spell on it. The moment the subject picks up or accepts that object its life force transfers to the gem with no save and no spell resistance.

trap-the-soul.notes: Two different trigger modes with different save behaviour, only one of which allows a save at all — a single save_gate would misrepresent whichever version was not chosen, so both are narrated.

effects.target: As arcane eye, except you fall asleep for the duration and the sensor — a dreamscryer — is invisible but exactly your size, shape and recognisably you, and cannot pass anywhere your body could not. Children up to about ten years old and animals can see it, and sleeping creatures sense it and may weave it into their dreams. Force effects and warding abjurations such as magic circle against evil block it regardless of your type or alignment. You wake if you dismiss the spell or the dreamscryer is dispelled or destroyed.

As teleport, except you may deliberately send any number of the creatures travelling with you into a mishap, or to a different location you visualise at the same time as the real destination, or both. A skill check to identify this spell identifies it as teleport instead.

treacherous-teleport.notes: No damage emitted. The only number teleport attaches to a mishap is the 1d10 in its mishap table, which is precisely the false conversion the brief names.

effects.target: Every object piled on a cloth — any amount or weight, so long as the pile fits within the cloth's dimensions up to a 10-foot cube — vanishes into the cloth and is replaced by an accurate sewn picture of the pile from any angle you choose. The cloth keeps its normal weight and size. You can restore the pile as a full-round action by unfurling the cloth and ending the spell, which consumes the cloth; anyone else must dispel the spell to do it. If the cloth is destroyed or badly damaged everything inside is lost. Artifacts and comparably unique objects are unaffected.

Even the closest inspection cannot tell you are a creature, though detect magic shows a faint transmutation. You see and hear everything around you as normal, your hit points and save bonuses are unchanged, and your clothing and gear change with you.
While in tree form your effective Dexterity score is 0 and your speed is 0 feet.

tree-shape.notes: Dexterity 0 and speed 0 are score replacements, not modifiers: ability_mod and speed both take a signed adjustment, so setting a score to zero cannot be expressed and is narrated. Dismissible as a free action rather than a standard action.

effects.target: Step into a living tree at least as thick as you are and teleport to another living tree of the same kind within range: 3,000 feet for oak, ash or yew; 2,000 feet for elm or linden; 1,500 feet for other deciduous trees; 1,000 feet for any conifer. Entering a tree tells you where every other tree of that kind within range is. Each transport is a full-round action, and you may enter a tree up to one time per caster level.
You may stay inside a tree without transporting, but are forced out when the spell ends. If the tree you are inside is chopped down or burned and you do not leave first, you are slain.

tree-stride.notes: Duration is 'hours/level or until expended' — the spell also ends the moment you step out of a tree, which the duration format cannot express, so it stays in the prose. The per-caster-level use limit has no home in the uses vocabulary either.

effects.target: The target is covered in burning acid and takes 1d6 points of acid damage and 1d6 points of fire damage each round. A successful Fortitude save that round halves the damage. Dousing the target in water ends both the acid and the fire; rolling on the ground extinguishes neither.

trial-of-fire-and-acid.notes: Both damage lines repeat every round, which the vocabulary has no type for, so neither is emitted as a damage spec and no scaling is emitted. The corpus already carries element=acid.

effects.target: As audiovisual hallucination, except the phantasm does nothing until a condition you set at casting occurs. You must beat the target's spell resistance to plant it, but the target makes no Will save to disbelieve until the trigger fires, at which point it gets an automatic Will save. The phantasm may carry sight, sound, smell, touch and temperature, including intelligible speech. The trigger may be as broad or as narrow as you like but must be something audible, tactile, olfactory or visual — never a quality that is not obvious to the senses, such as alignment — and the spell watches for it through the target's own senses.

triggered-hallucination.notes: Duration is 'permanent until triggered, then minutes/level (1)': the waiting phase is until_discharged, and the 1 minute/level that follows the trigger cannot be expressed as a second phase, so it is recorded here.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: As suggestion, except the suggestion may only specify a condition that triggers a particular activity, and the subject does not remember being given it until the trigger occurs.

triggered-suggestion.notes: Duration is 'days/level (1) or until discharged'; only the outer bound fits the format, so the discharge is noted here. Language-dependent and mind-affecting.

effects.target: appraise
Attempt an Appraise check to determine an object's value as a move action, and take 10 on an Appraise check even when stress or distraction would normally forbid it.
You know when you have failed an Appraise check, and you never arrive at a wildly inaccurate price.

Creates a completely real, nonmagical, unattended object of any material, up to 1 cubic foot per caster level. Complex items require successful Craft checks. Objects made this way can serve as material components.

true-creation.notes: Ten minute casting time. Unlike ordinary conjured matter this is permanent and real, which is why the duration is instantaneous rather than a timed effect.

effects.target: Strips any polymorph effect from up to one creature per 3 caster levels, none more than 30 feet apart, returning each to its true form even against its will. Against a polymorph spell effect such as baleful polymorph or giant form you make a caster level check (1d20 + caster level, maximum +15) against DC 11 + the effect's caster level; success ends the polymorph immediately.

A creature with a supernatural change-shape ability, such as a lycanthrope, must make a Will save or revert to its true form at once. If it fails, it may try a second Will save as a full-round action that does not provoke; success ends the spell and it can change shape again, failure locks it in its true form for the duration and blocks any further polymorph effect.

true-form.notes: Not modelled as a save_gate: there are two different resistances here — a caster level check against spell polymorphs and a two-stage Will save against supernatural shapechangers — and a single gate would apply the wrong one to half the cases.

effects.target: As divination, except it can look up to 100 years into the future. Answers about events that distant are extremely cryptic.

As raise dead, except the creature may have been dead as long as 10 years per caster level, and even a destroyed body works so long as you identify the deceased unambiguously, such as by reciting their time and place of birth or death. The creature returns at full hit points, vigour and health, with no negative levels or lost Constitution, and with every spell it had prepared when it died.
It can restore someone slain by a death effect, or someone made undead and then destroyed, and works on elementals and outsiders, but never on constructs, undead, or anyone who died of old age.

true-resurrection.notes: 'Restored to full hit points' is not a dice value and heal takes dice, so it is not emitted as a heal spec — restoring a creature to its maximum is a different operation from healing a stated amount.

effects.target: true_seeing

The subject sees through normal and magical darkness, spots magically hidden secret doors, pinpoints creatures under blur or displacement, sees invisible things normally, sees through illusions, sees the true form of anything polymorphed or transmuted, and can focus its sight into the Ethereal Plane, though not into extradimensional spaces.

It does not see through solid objects, is not X-ray vision, does not negate concealment such as fog, and does not defeat mundane disguises, creatures merely hiding, or secret doors hidden by mundane means. It also cannot be combined with other magic — no true seeing through a crystal ball or alongside clairaudience/clairvoyance.
Choose one skill as you cast. The next check you attempt with that skill before the duration ends gains an insight bonus equal to half your caster level (minimum 1).

true-skill.notes: The bonus is half caster level, and skill_mod's amount is an integer, so a level-scaled modifier cannot be expressed. Also, the skill is chosen at casting rather than fixed by the spell, which skill_mod's target vocabulary cannot represent either. Both are real vocabulary gaps.

effects.note: Applies to your next single attack roll, if it is made before the end of the next round.

effects.target: Ignore the miss chance that normally applies to an attacker striking a concealed target, for that attack.

true-strike.notes: Duration is 'see text' and the text gives a window — 'before the end of the next round' — rather than a length. That is a deadline for one use, not a duration, so none is emitted and the uses field carries the single use instead.

effects.target: Speak with any creature that is not mindless: anyone who can hear you understands you as though you spoke their language or natural mode of communication, and you hear their replies in your own native tongue.
